"THE ELDER REALMS: A RETRO FANTASY RPG

ULTIMATE MASTER GAME CREATION PROMPT

Create an immersive, playable, first-person, 3D medieval fantasy RPG for mobile devices. The game should capture the atmosphere, freedom, exploration, character development, and adventure of classic open-world RPGs such as The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim and The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind, combined with the distinctive retro 3D visual style of Doom 64 and classic Doom.

This is an original fantasy RPG, not a remake of any existing game.

The objective is to create a compact but immersive open-world adventure where the player can create a unique character, explore a mysterious fantasy world, fight monsters, discover ancient ruins, interact with inhabitants, complete quests, collect equipment, learn magic, and become stronger.

IMPORTANT: Gameplay functionality, exploration, and immersion are more important than graphical quality or excessive world size.

1. VISUAL IDENTITY AND GRAPHICAL STYLE

The game must have a distinctive retro 3D aesthetic.

Use these artistic references:

- Doom 64: dark atmosphere, pixelated textures, dramatic lighting, mysterious environments.
- Classic Doom: recognizable low-poly 3D geometry and retro first-person presentation.
- Morrowind: medieval fantasy architecture, strange landscapes, mysterious creatures, and immersive world design.
- Early 2000s fantasy RPGs: simple but atmospheric 3D models and environments.

Visual requirements:

- Fully three-dimensional environments and characters.
- Low-poly models.
- Pixelated, low-resolution textures.
- Retro texture filtering.
- Simple but recognizable character models.
- Medieval fantasy architecture.
- Atmospheric forests, mountains, caves, ruins, villages, and castles.
- Dark dungeons and mysterious underground locations.
- Atmospheric fog, shadows, and lighting.
- Retro-inspired weapons, armor, monsters, and magical effects.

The game must look intentionally retro, not unfinished or randomly assembled.

Do not use photorealistic graphics. Do not use 2D pixel art. The world must be genuinely 3D.

Create an atmospheric world that feels like an old fantasy RPG running on early 3D gaming hardware.

2. THE WORLD

Create an original medieval fantasy world called AETHORIA.

Aethoria is an ancient kingdom filled with forgotten civilizations, dangerous creatures, abandoned settlements, mysterious forests, and ancient magical ruins.

The kingdom is experiencing a period of instability. Ancient powers are awakening beneath the land, monsters are appearing in previously safe regions, and different settlements are struggling to survive.

The player arrives in this world as a new adventurer whose decisions and discoveries gradually reveal the history of the kingdom.

Create a connected, moderately sized open world.

Include:

- One main medieval city with merchants, buildings, guards, and important NPCs.
- One smaller town.
- Three villages.
- A large forest.
- A mountainous region.
- Open plains.
- Ancient ruins.
- Underground caves.
- An abandoned fortress.
- Hidden locations and treasure.

The world should encourage exploration. The player must be able to leave the main roads, discover unexpected locations, fight enemies, find treasure, and explore without constantly following the main storyline.

Avoid an enormous or empty map. Every location should have a purpose.

3. CHARACTER CREATION

Character creation is one of the most important features.

Before starting the adventure, allow the player to create a character.

Include four playable races:

HUMAN
Balanced attributes, adaptable and versatile.

ELF
Greater magical potential, agility, and precision.

ORC
Greater physical strength, health, and melee damage.

DWARF
Greater endurance, resistance, and defensive capabilities.

Each race must have a distinct appearance, physical proportions, and gameplay bonuses.

Physical customization

Allow actual visual customization of the 3D character.

Include:

- Skin color.
- Face shape.
- Eye color.
- Hair style.
- Hair color.
- Facial hair where applicable.
- Body type.
- Height.
- Physical proportions.

Customization must visibly change the character model, not merely change a portrait or display a selection icon.

Preserve the selected appearance throughout the game.

4. CHARACTER CLASSES

Allow the player to select one of five classes.

WARRIOR
Specializes in swords, axes, shields, heavy armor, and physical damage.

MAGE
Specializes in offensive magic, defensive spells, magical energy, and staffs.

ARCHER
Specializes in bows, ranged attacks, precision, and distance combat.

ASSASSIN
Specializes in daggers, stealth, speed, and critical attacks.

PALADIN
Specializes in swords, shields, healing magic, protection, and defense.

Classes must have meaningful gameplay differences, unique starting attributes, and appropriate starting equipment.

5. FIRST-PERSON GAMEPLAY

The entire adventure should be experienced primarily in first person.

Implement:

- First-person movement.
- Walking and running.
- Jumping.
- Mouse-style or touchscreen camera rotation.
- Weapon visibility.
- Functional attacks.
- Spellcasting.
- Object interaction.
- Doors and containers.
- NPC interaction.
- Character and inventory menus.

Movement and camera controls must feel responsive.

The player should feel physically present in the environment.

6. COMBAT AND MAGIC

Create real-time combat.

Include:

- Sword attacks.
- Axe attacks.
- Dagger attacks.
- Bow shooting.
- Shield blocking.
- Enemy attacks.
- Damage calculation.
- Health and death systems.
- Hit detection.
- Combat animations or suitable visual equivalents.

Include functional magical abilities:

- Fireball.
- Ice projectile.
- Healing.
- Magical protection.

Weapons and spells must produce real gameplay effects.

Combat should be challenging but fair.

7. ENEMIES AND CREATURES

Include five initial enemy types:

1. Bandits.
2. Wolves.
3. Skeletons.
4. Giant spiders.
5. Trolls.

Every enemy should have recognizable 3D models, health, attacks, movement, and basic AI.

Enemies should detect the player, pursue them, attack, and react to damage.

Place enemies appropriately throughout the world.

8. CHARACTER PROGRESSION

Implement a genuine RPG progression system.

Include:

- Experience points.
- Character levels.
- Health.
- Stamina.
- Magicka.
- Strength.
- Agility.
- Defense.
- Magical power.
- Class-related abilities.

The player should gain experience by defeating enemies, completing quests, and exploring.

Leveling up must improve the character and provide a sense of progression.

9. INVENTORY AND EQUIPMENT

Create a functional inventory.

Include:

- Swords.
- Axes.
- Daggers.
- Bows.
- Shields.
- Armor.
- Magical staffs.
- Potions.
- Consumables.
- Quest objects.
- Treasure.

Allow the player to collect, inspect, equip, unequip, and use items.

Weapons must affect damage. Armor must affect defense. Potions must produce their intended effects.

Include merchants who sell and purchase equipment.

10. NPCS AND QUESTS

Create inhabitants throughout the world.

Include:

- Merchants.
- Guards.
- Villagers.
- Adventurers.
- Quest-giving characters.
- Important storyline characters.

NPCs must have names, basic identities, and functional dialogue interactions.

Create:

- One main storyline.
- Five secondary quests.
- Quest objectives.
- Quest rewards.
- A simple quest journal.

The storyline should involve the awakening of an ancient power beneath Aethoria.

The player should discover the truth through exploration, dialogue, and completing missions.

Do not create complicated political simulations or unnecessarily sophisticated NPC systems.

11. MOBILE INTERFACE

Design the game specifically for Android touchscreen devices.

Include:

- Virtual joystick on the left.
- Touch camera control on the right.
- Attack button.
- Block button.
- Jump button.
- Interaction button.
- Magic button.
- Inventory button.
- Character menu.
- Quest journal.
- Health, stamina, and magicka indicators.

Controls must be functional and comfortable on a mobile screen.

Allow the player to explore and fight without requiring a keyboard or physical controller.

12. IMMERSION AND ATMOSPHERE

The world should feel mysterious, ancient, and dangerous.

Use:

- Atmospheric environmental sounds.
- Footsteps.
- Weapon sounds.
- Monster sounds.
- Ambient forest and village sounds.
- Dungeon atmosphere.
- Music appropriate to medieval fantasy.

Create a sense of discovery and adventure.

The player should feel that the world exists beyond the main quest.

13. TECHNICAL AND PERFORMANCE PRIORITIES

The game must be designed for Android.

Prioritize:

- Stable performance.
- Responsive touchscreen controls.
- Efficient 3D models.
- Lightweight textures.
- Simple lighting.
- Efficient environments.
- Reliable saving and loading.
- Offline gameplay whenever supported.

Use the development capabilities and tools available in AI Game Maker.

Do not introduce unnecessary programming frameworks, external systems, or unsupported technologies.

If a feature cannot be implemented exactly as described, create the simplest functional alternative.

14. DEVELOPMENT AND FUNCTIONALITY RULES

These rules are essential:

- Create an actual playable game, not a static demonstration.
- Every visible button must perform its intended action.
- Character customization must change the character's appearance.
- Different races must have actual gameplay differences.
- Classes must affect gameplay.
- Combat must calculate damage.
- Enemies must be capable of attacking the player.
- Experience and leveling must work.
- Inventory and equipment must work.
- Quests must have actual objectives and completion conditions.
- Player progress and character appearance should be preserved through saving whenever supported.
- Do not display features as completed if they are not functional.
- Avoid unnecessary complexity that could prevent the game from working.

If the application cannot create all systems simultaneously, prioritize the essential playable experience: character creation, first-person movement, exploration, combat, and character progression.

Expand the game without breaking existing functionality.

15. FINAL GAME EXPERIENCE

The finished game should feel like a classic first-person fantasy RPG rediscovered from the early 2000s.

The player must be able to:

1. Create and customize a unique character.
2. Choose a race and class.
3. Enter a mysterious medieval fantasy world.
4. Explore villages, forests, mountains, caves, and ruins.
5. Encounter and fight dangerous creatures.
6. Use weapons, shields, bows, and magic.
7. Interact with inhabitants.
8. Accept and complete quests.
9. Discover treasure and equipment.
10. Improve attributes and abilities.
11. Develop their own playstyle.
12. Explore freely and discover secrets.

The experience should prioritize freedom, exploration, atmosphere, character identity, and meaningful progression.

FINAL DIRECTIVE: Create a coherent, immersive, functional retro 3D open-world fantasy RPG. Prioritize a smaller but complete and enjoyable adventure over a massive unfinished world. Every implemented feature must serve the actual gameplay experience.
"

"THE ELDER REALMS: A RETRO FANTASY RPG

ULTIMATE MASTER GAME CREATION PROMPT

Create an immersive, playable, first-person, 3D medieval fantasy RPG for mobile devices. The game should capture the atmosphere, freedom, exploration, character development, and adventure of classic open-world RPGs such as The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim and The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind, combined with the distinctive retro 3D visual style of Doom 64 and classic Doom.

This is an original fantasy RPG, not a remake of any existing game.

The objective is to create a compact but immersive open-world adventure where the player can create a unique character, explore a mysterious fantasy world, fight monsters, discover ancient ruins, interact with inhabitants, complete quests, collect equipment, learn magic, and become stronger.

IMPORTANT: Gameplay functionality, exploration, and immersion are more important than graphical quality or excessive world size.

1. VISUAL IDENTITY AND GRAPHICAL STYLE

The game must have a distinctive retro 3D aesthetic.

Use these artistic references:

- Doom 64: dark atmosphere, pixelated textures, dramatic lighting, mysterious environments.
- Classic Doom: recognizable low-poly 3D geometry and retro first-person presentation.
- Morrowind: medieval fantasy architecture, strange landscapes, mysterious creatures, and immersive world design.
- Early 2000s fantasy RPGs: simple but atmospheric 3D models and environments.

Visual requirements:

- Fully three-dimensional environments and characters.
- Low-poly models.
- Pixelated, low-resolution textures.
- Retro texture filtering.
- Simple but recognizable character models.
- Medieval fantasy architecture.
- Atmospheric forests, mountains, caves, ruins, villages, and castles.
- Dark dungeons and mysterious underground locations.
- Atmospheric fog, shadows, and lighting.
- Retro-inspired weapons, armor, monsters, and magical effects.

The game must look intentionally retro, not unfinished or randomly assembled.

Do not use photorealistic graphics. Do not use 2D pixel art. The world must be genuinely 3D.

Create an atmospheric world that feels like an old fantasy RPG running on early 3D gaming hardware.

2. THE WORLD

Create an original medieval fantasy world called AETHORIA.

Aethoria is an ancient kingdom filled with forgotten civilizations, dangerous creatures, abandoned settlements, mysterious forests, and ancient magical ruins.

The kingdom is experiencing a period of instability. Ancient powers are awakening beneath the land, monsters are appearing in previously safe regions, and different settlements are struggling to survive.

The player arrives in this world as a new adventurer whose decisions and discoveries gradually reveal the history of the kingdom.

Create a connected, moderately sized open world.

Include:

- One main medieval city with merchants, buildings, guards, and important NPCs.
- One smaller town.
- Three villages.
- A large forest.
- A mountainous region.
- Open plains.
- Ancient ruins.
- Underground caves.
- An abandoned fortress.
- Hidden locations and treasure.

The world should encourage exploration. The player must be able to leave the main roads, discover unexpected locations, fight enemies, find treasure, and explore without constantly following the main storyline.

Avoid an enormous or empty map. Every location should have a purpose.

3. CHARACTER CREATION

Character creation is one of the most important features.

Before starting the adventure, allow the player to create a character.

Include four playable races:

HUMAN
Balanced attributes, adaptable and versatile.

ELF
Greater magical potential, agility, and precision.

ORC
Greater physical strength, health, and melee damage.

DWARF
Greater endurance, resistance, and defensive capabilities.

Each race must have a distinct appearance, physical proportions, and gameplay bonuses.

Physical customization

Allow actual visual customization of the 3D character.

Include:

- Skin color.
- Face shape.
- Eye color.
- Hair style.
- Hair color.
- Facial hair where applicable.
- Body type.
- Height.
- Physical proportions.

Customization must visibly change the character model, not merely change a portrait or display a selection icon.

Preserve the selected appearance throughout the game.

4. CHARACTER CLASSES

Allow the player to select one of five classes.

WARRIOR
Specializes in swords, axes, shields, heavy armor, and physical damage.

MAGE
Specializes in offensive magic, defensive spells, magical energy, and staffs.

ARCHER
Specializes in bows, ranged attacks, precision, and distance combat.

ASSASSIN
Specializes in daggers, stealth, speed, and critical attacks.

PALADIN
Specializes in swords, shields, healing magic, protection, and defense.

Classes must have meaningful gameplay differences, unique starting attributes, and appropriate starting equipment.

5. FIRST-PERSON GAMEPLAY

The entire adventure should be experienced primarily in first person.

Implement:

- First-person movement.
- Walking and running.
- Jumping.
- Mouse-style or touchscreen camera rotation.
- Weapon visibility.
- Functional attacks.
- Spellcasting.
- Object interaction.
- Doors and containers.
- NPC interaction.
- Character and inventory menus.

Movement and camera controls must feel responsive.

The player should feel physically present in the environment.

6. COMBAT AND MAGIC

Create real-time combat.

Include:

- Sword attacks.
- Axe attacks.
- Dagger attacks.
- Bow shooting.
- Shield blocking.
- Enemy attacks.
- Damage calculation.
- Health and death systems.
- Hit detection.
- Combat animations or suitable visual equivalents.

Include functional magical abilities:

- Fireball.
- Ice projectile.
- Healing.
- Magical protection.

Weapons and spells must produce real gameplay effects.

Combat should be challenging but fair.

7. ENEMIES AND CREATURES

Include five initial enemy types:

1. Bandits.
2. Wolves.
3. Skeletons.
4. Giant spiders.
5. Trolls.

Every enemy should have recognizable 3D models, health, attacks, movement, and basic AI.

Enemies should detect the player, pursue them, attack, and react to damage.

Place enemies appropriately throughout the world.

8. CHARACTER PROGRESSION

Implement a genuine RPG progression system.

Include:

- Experience points.
- Character levels.
- Health.
- Stamina.
- Magicka.
- Strength.
- Agility.
- Defense.
- Magical power.
- Class-related abilities.

The player should gain experience by defeating enemies, completing quests, and exploring.

Leveling up must improve the character and provide a sense of progression.

9. INVENTORY AND EQUIPMENT

Create a functional inventory.

Include:

- Swords.
- Axes.
- Daggers.
- Bows.
- Shields.
- Armor.
- Magical staffs.
- Potions.
- Consumables.
- Quest objects.
- Treasure.

Allow the player to collect, inspect, equip, unequip, and use items.

Weapons must affect damage. Armor must affect defense. Potions must produce their intended effects.

Include merchants who sell and purchase equipment.

10. NPCS AND QUESTS

Create inhabitants throughout the world.

Include:

- Merchants.
- Guards.
- Villagers.
- Adventurers.
- Quest-giving characters.
- Important storyline characters.

NPCs must have names, basic identities, and functional dialogue interactions.

Create:

- One main storyline.
- Five secondary quests.
- Quest objectives.
- Quest rewards.
- A simple quest journal.

The storyline should involve the awakening of an ancient power beneath Aethoria.

The player should discover the truth through exploration, dialogue, and completing missions.

Do not create complicated political simulations or unnecessarily sophisticated NPC systems.

11. MOBILE INTERFACE

Design the game specifically for Android touchscreen devices.

Include:

- Virtual joystick on the left.
- Touch camera control on the right.
- Attack button.
- Block button.
- Jump button.
- Interaction button.
- Magic button.
- Inventory button.
- Character menu.
- Quest journal.
- Health, stamina, and magicka indicators.

Controls must be functional and comfortable on a mobile screen.

Allow the player to explore and fight without requiring a keyboard or physical controller.
